newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resid prices mixed, NYH HSFO gains.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resid prices mixed, NYH HSFO gains.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices were mixed Wednesday in lackluster activity, with firmer bunkers propping up high sulphur grades, while ample supply pressured some low sulphurs, industry sources said.

"The Merc was up pretty big and bunkers were up, which helped high sulphur," said one cash trader, noting low sulphur seemed a bit soft on ample avails despite better East Coast utility demand from the weather.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent eased slightly to about the $18 a barrel level after reports a mid-Feb cargo sold at $17.65, traders said.

NYH February paper was talked little changed in the $17.50-75 area. Traders said a New England utility, which bought one percent earlier this week, may be out for another small piece soon due to rising burns on the latest cold wave.

NYH 0.3 percent high pour edged up slightly to $19.25. One trader said NYPA did not award its 200,000-barrel HP tender because suppliers could not deliver by Feb 3-7. The utility may reissue the tender tomorrow but this was not confirmed.
High sulphurs in New York, again helped by firmer bunkers, were up slightly, with 2.2 percent near $17, traders said.
Cold weather in the East again boosted New York city gate gas prices by another 20 cents to the $3.80/mmBtu level. NYH one percent resid remained at a $2.85/mmBtu equivalent.
